fields.description:
## Context / Problem
A single Gerrit Verified run needs 21 concurrent job slots. The navapbc org is on GitHub Free: 20 total concurrent jobs and 5 concurrent macOS, enforced PER ORGANIZATION and shared with every other navapbc repo. So one run, in an otherwise idle org, cannot fully parallelize; under a 6-change burst later runs queued 6.7-8.4m for a macOS slot, which is what turns a ~21m run into the 41-47m seen from Gerrit.

`.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` fans out 5 `per-extra` matrix cells plus a `union` cell — 6 jobs, each doing 0.4-0.8m of real work while holding a slot for a full checkout + setup-python + install.

(The redundant `import-linter` job is handled separately in ticket 2132-e48f-425c-4f24; this ticket does not touch it.)

## Approach
Collapse the 5 `per-extra` cells + `union` into ONE job running a venv loop.

ITERATIONS. Five-plus-one is WRONG as originally drafted, because the current matrix list and `_optional.EXTRAS` are not the same set. Verified: `_optional.EXTRAS == {agents, eval, grounding, metrics, tracing}` while the matrix runs `{agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding}`. So:
- `mcp` is NOT in `_optional.EXTRAS` — it is the server transport, has no detection probe, and is validated by its boot check instead.
- `metrics` IS in `_optional.EXTRAS` and has NO per-extra CI today — a real pre-existing gap the loop closes for free.
The loop therefore runs over `_optional.EXTRAS` keys UNION `{mcp}` = six isolation iterations, PLUS one UNION iteration installing `.[agents,eval,tracing]` jointly into a single venv. The union is not redundant with the isolation runs: it is the only thing exercising JOINT dependency resolution and can surface a `ResolutionImpossible` no single-extra install can.

PER-ITERATION WORK must reproduce everything the current cells do, not just the install:
- `import rebar` with the extra present;
- for extras in `_optional.EXTRAS`, assert `_optional.extra_installed(extra)` (the detection probe);
- `rebar-mcp --help` for the mcp iteration ONLY, reproducing today's `if: matrix.extra == 'mcp'`. Running it everywhere fails in venvs lacking the entry point; dropping it silently weakens the mcp boot check.

TWO ABSOLUTE RULES, each guarding a silent-failure mode:
- NEVER `source .../activate`. Activations STACK across iterations, so PATH decides which interpreter runs and every iteration can silently re-test extra #1.
- ALWAYS invoke by absolute path (`"$v/bin/python"`, `"$v/bin/rebar-mcp"`). A bare `python`/`rebar-mcp` runs the AMBIENT interpreter and can pass while testing nothing. Today's `rebar-mcp --help` (_optionality.yml:178-180) is exactly such a bare console-script call and must be rewritten.

ERROR ISOLATION is explicit because Actions runs `run:` under `bash -e`: a naive loop dies on the first failure (losing today's `fail-fast: false` diagnostics), while `|| true`/`set +e` without aggregation makes the whole contract a no-op that ALWAYS PASSES. Use an `rc` accumulator — guard each iteration with `|| { rc=1; echo "::error::<extra> failed"; continue; }` and end the step with `exit $rc`.

VENV HYGIENE: `python -m venv` from a `setup-python` interpreter is already clean (user site-packages disabled, `include-system-site-packages=false`), and `PYTHONPATH`/`PIP_*` are unset in both workflows, so `--copies`/`PYTHONNOUSERSITE`/`--without-pip` are NOT needed. The pip HTTP cache shared across venvs is a speed benefit only (wheels are content-addressed). Run `pip install --upgrade pip` per venv (ensurepip ships an old pip).

KEEP `clean-core-wheel` byte-identical. It is the check this file header credits with catching "the module-scope-import class that escaped once", it builds a real wheel, and it is the ONLY lane where `agents_extra_installed()` is False — which is what makes its skipif-degradation tests actually execute.

Rejected: sequential `pip install .[agents]` then `.[eval]` into one shared python — after the first install the env is contaminated, so a missing dependency declaration in a later extra PASSES silently; that is the exact bug class this workflow exists to catch. Rejected: per-extra venvs with no union iteration (loses joint resolution). Rejected: collapsing `clean-core-wheel` in. Considered and not chosen: `strategy: {max-parallel: 1}` on the existing matrix (5->1 peak slots, zero new bash) — the loop was chosen deliberately for the larger slot saving.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` — replace the `per-extra` matrix job and the `union` job with the single venv-loop job.
- `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` — durable guards on the loop shape and extras coverage.
- `infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json` — it hard-codes the doomed check names (`extra "agents" installs`, `union [agents,eval,tracing] resolves`, ...). It is not the live ruleset (that is Terraform `gerrit-mirror-lock-main`, which declares no `required_status_checks`), but it IS POSTed back by `infra/github/rollback-mirror-lock.sh:75-88` — so leaving it stale means an emergency rollback would demand checks that cannot exist and would freeze `main`.

NOT in scope: `import-linter` (ticket 2132), `clean-core-wheel`, `_build-and-test.yml`, `gerrit-verify.yaml`.

## Testing
Durable checked-in guards, not one-time manual observations, because the risk is a later careless edit:
- assert the loop step text contains the `rc` accumulator shape (`continue` and `exit $rc`) and contains NO `activate`, so the swallowed-failure and stacked-activation footguns cannot be reintroduced silently;
- assert every key in `_optional.EXTRAS` appears in the looped extra list, so a newly declared extra cannot ship with zero CI.

Workflow-level validation: `optionality.yml` triggers on `push`, so pushing a scratch branch to the GitHub mirror exercises the modified reusable end-to-end. A PULL REQUEST does NOT work — `.github/workflows/lockdown.yml` runs `dessant/repo-lockdown` on `pull_request_target` with `close-pr: true` (only dependabot exempt), so the mirror auto-closes PRs. `workflow_dispatch` on `optionality.yml` is the fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each isolation extra installs into its own freshly-created venv, never one that already had another extra installed.
- [ ] The isolation iteration set equals `_optional.EXTRAS` keys plus `mcp`, so `metrics` gains per-extra CI it does not have today.
- [ ] A UNION iteration installs `.[agents,eval,tracing]` jointly into one venv.
- [ ] Each isolation iteration runs `import rebar` and, for extras in `_optional.EXTRAS`, asserts `_optional.extra_installed(extra)`.
- [ ] `rebar-mcp --help` runs for the mcp iteration only, invoked by absolute venv path.
- [ ] Every interpreter/console-script call in the loop uses an absolute `"$v/bin/..."` path, and the loop contains no `activate`.
- [ ] The loop uses an `rc` accumulator with `continue` and exits non-zero if any iteration failed.
- [ ] A checked-in test asserts the loop step contains `exit $rc` and `continue` and no `activate`.
- [ ] A checked-in test asserts the looped extra list covers every key in `_optional.EXTRAS`.
- [ ] `clean-core-wheel` is byte-identical to its current form.
- [ ] `infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json` no longer names removed checks.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py` and `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` pass.
- [ ] `make lint` passes (actionlint covers all workflows).
